newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes weak as June overhang hits sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes weak as June overhang hits sentiment.

text.p: Sentiment on the Middle East crude market remains bearish amid lacklustre interest.
There were still June cargoes of Abu Dhabi grades heard available, keeping buyers relaxed about covering July requirements in expectation the overhang would impact July pricing.
A European major was heard to have one million barrels of June Murban, which it was planning to take to Africa. The major would not confirm this, saying only it "was doing something internally."
The only July offer was on Oman.
A shosha was looking to sell a cargo at MPM -5 cents per barrel. But no firm buyers were seen.
Prices of heavy Indonesian crudes were also slipping. A Japanese refiner bought a parcel of Minas on Wednesday at ICP +11/15 cents. This was half the premium achieved by Minas sellers a week ago.
There were also rumours a western trader was taking one million barrels of Widuri, loading end May, to the U.S. Gulf Coast for refining.
This could take some length out of the market, but traders said there was still ample supplies of Widuri available in June.
They said Asian demand was slack and so sellers were looking to sell to the US.
The overnight rise in Brent pushed Tapis swaps up marginally. June paper Tapis was discussed at $21.35-$21.45 per barrel, up five cents on the day.
